what_its_for: Dronabinol is used to treat nausea and vomiting caused by cancer chemotherapy when other anti-nausea medicines have not worked. It is also used to help improve appetite and prevent weight loss in people with AIDS. Dronabinol is a man-made form of THC, the active ingredient found in cannabis (marijuana).
how_to_take: Dronabinol capsules (Marinol) are taken by mouth and can be swallowed whole. The liquid form (Syndros) is also taken by mouth using the special measuring device provided — never use a regular household spoon. Take it exactly as your doctor prescribes. Do not take more than prescribed, as this medicine can affect your thinking and behavior. You may take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time.
dosing: For nausea and vomiting: The usual dose is taken 1 to 3 hours before chemotherapy and then every 2 to 4 hours after chemotherapy, for up to 4 to 6 doses per day. For appetite problems in AIDS: It is usually taken twice a day, before lunch and dinner. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and slowly increase it. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is not too close to the time of your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store Marinol capsules in the refrigerator (between 46°F and 59°F / 8°C and 15°C). You may also store them at cool room temperature (below 77°F / 25°C) for short periods. Store Syndros liquid in the refrigerator and use it within 28 days of opening. Keep the bottle tightly closed and protect it from light. Keep all forms of dronabinol away from heat and out of reach of children. Do not freeze.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking dronabinol — it can increase dizziness, confusion, and sedation. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be alert and clear-headed until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other sedating medicines, sleep aids, anxiety medicines, or opioid pain relievers unless your doctor approves. Do not use marijuana or cannabis products while on this medication. Avoid making important decisions while taking this medicine, as it may affect your judgment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: fast or pounding heartbeat, chest pain, fainting, or feeling like you might pass out; severe confusion, paranoia, hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), or unusual thoughts; severe dizziness or loss of balance; mood changes such as anxiety, depression, or thoughts of self-harm; seizures; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, trouble breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, or throat. Also call your doctor if your nausea, vomiting, or appetite problems are not improving.
when_it_works: For nausea and vomiting, dronabinol usually starts working within 30 minutes to 1 hour after you take it. For improving appetite in AIDS patients, it may take a few days to a few weeks before you notice a meaningful improvement. Keep taking it as directed even if you do not feel effects right away.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with extra caution. Older patients are more sensitive to the mental and blood pressure effects of this medicine and may experience more side effects like dizziness, confusion, and falls. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established for appetite stimulation. For nausea from chemotherapy, it has been used in children but requires careful dose monitoring. Pregnancy: Dronabinol is not recommended during pregnancy. Cannabis compounds may harm an unborn baby. Talk to your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking dronabinol, as it may pass into breast milk and harm a nursing infant. Liver disease: Use with caution, as the drug is processed by the liver. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose.
